newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark dip under 1.6340 no risk to rally.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/mark dip under 1.6340 no risk to rally.

text.p: Although important support at 1.6340 marks was violated on Thursday, the dollar's losses were limited and the ongoing retreat from this week's 31-month high should not jeopardize the overall rally, chartists said.
"I don't think it's anything fatal," said Stephanie Davis, technical analyst at Technical Data. "You could go all the way down to 1.62 through 1.6240 marks without any big problem.
The dollar barely stumbled in its near four-week sprint to a 1.6570 peak versus the mark on Tuesday, so it was overdue for a breather, analysts said.
Ture Johnson, technical analyst at Bank of America said the dollar's push below Wednesday's low near 1.6340 could open up the 1.6280 to 1.6240 mark region.
"But then you buy it down there," he added.
The dollar fell to 1.6318 marks before steadying on Thursday. At 1500 EST/2000 GMT, it was quoted at 1.6350/60 marks, down from 1.6410/15 marks at the U.S. open.
Johnson placed minor resistance at 1.6420/30 followed by 1.65 marks. A close above 1.6570 would be the key bullish signal for dollar/mark, he said.
Versus the yen, consolidation is also the name of the game and the big picture remains decidedly bullish, analysts said.
Long-term technical oscillators point higher and the dollar is still trading above its 10- and 50-month moving averages, Davis said.
Short-term support near 120.90 yen may protect the downside, chartists said. But a drop to 120.00/15 should not extinguish the rally, they added.
In the medium term, technicians said the dollar could reach 1.6750 to 1.68 marks and 124 to 126 yen before the rally fizzles.
But by the end of the year, the dollar could go well above 1.68 marks and 126 yen, they said.
"As long as the trend remains up on the weekly and monthly charts, we're very positive for the dollar," Johnson said.
At 1500 EST dollar/yen was trading at 121.55/65, down from 121.80/90 at the open.
